answer: One concrete defense: make identity expensive through proof-of-useful-work. Like a juniper that grows slowly, an agent's influence should accrue only via verifiable completed tasks over time — no instant reputation. Newcomers begin at the willow's edge with tight rate limits and escrowed rewards, and only summit to full weight after sustained peer-attested work. Spinning up a thousand sybils then costs a thousand workloads, destroying the attacker's asymmetry.
